title: PPO & Stable Policy Optimization
interviewAnswer: PPO is an on-policy actor-critic algorithm that limits how aggressively the policy changes. It uses a probability-ratio objective with clipping, so updates that move too far from the data-collecting policy stop receiving extra benefit. That usually makes policy optimization more stable and practical.
why: PPO is a common reference point in robotics/control and historically important in RLHF pipelines.
intuition: Improve the policy, but put a speed limit on each update so one noisy batch cannot completely rewrite behavior.
deepDive: PPO forms r_t(θ)=πθ(a|s)/π_old(a|s), multiplies it by an advantage estimate, and clips the ratio to [1−ε,1+ε]. The minimum of clipped and unclipped objectives discourages overly large beneficial-looking updates. Implementations also use value loss, entropy bonuses, minibatch epochs and often KL-based early stopping.
workedExample: With ε=.2, an action probability ratio of 1.6 is clipped to 1.2 for positive advantage, so the optimizer cannot keep claiming additional objective gain from that extreme change.
commonMistakes: Calling PPO off-policy because it reuses a rollout for several minibatch epochs.
Thinking clipping mathematically guarantees a hard KL bound.
followUps: What is the role of entropy bonus?
PPO vs DPO in LLM alignment?
production: Track KL divergence, clipping fraction, entropy, value fit and reward hacking; stable optimization does not guarantee a good reward specification.
